messages.subject: sliderInput formatting
parts:
This example

shinyApp(
    ui = sliderInput("xbar", NULL, 7.4945, 9.4066, 8.45, .03, animate=list(interval=2000), width="150px"),
  server=function(input, output) {
  })


produces a slider with limits
7.4,945  and 9.4,066
where it is apparently counting to the left from the end of the number.

How can I tell it to suppress the "," and use
7.4945  and 9.4066


And I don't really want this, but how can I tell it to put the ","
counting to the right of the decimal point so it would give
7.494,5  and 9.406,6

Rich

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: sliderInput formatting
parts:
Regarding the main question: that's strange, I haven't noticed that before.  It seems like it's treating the value to the right of the decimal as an integer, and inserts commas as if it was a regular number. It looks like `sliderInput` has a `sep` parameter that is a comma by default, so if you supply `sep = ""`, it will fix that.  BUT that will also affect the number to the left of the decimal, so if you have numbers that are greater than 1000, they will not be formatted with commas.  Seems like a bug to me. Maybe someone else can shed some more light on this.

 sliderInput("xbar", NULL, 7.4945, 9.4066, 8.45, .03, animate=list(interval=2000), width="150px", sep = "")
